note: ⛔ SNG-356 — THE AUTHORED SUB-ATTRIBUTE LADDER (Erik ratified 2026-08-07: 'specify what each point up to 20 gets you so we can better control the impact and the player can see it exactly'). Every rank's grant is AUTHORED HERE, not computed in code — so it is tunable without a build, inspectable by the player, and gated like the rest of the content pack (Design Law 15). RETROACTIVE by Erik's direction: existing characters recompute from their current sub values; nothing is refunded or respent. ⚠️ THIS FILE RETIRES `attributeSoftCap`. The soft cap bent the curve at rank 4 — measured against real saves (SNG-354), rank 4 is the TOP OF EARLY GAME, exactly where a player still needs base competence. The `roll` column below bends at rank 6 instead, which is mid-game, where 'you have the basics, now specialise' is actually true. `roll` is CUMULATIVE-BY-SUMMING the per-rank values. ⛔ ROLL COLUMN RATIFIED BY ERIK 2026-08-07 ON HARNESS EVIDENCE (SNG-357). The gate this file set for itself is satisfied: run against Silas Weir's real spread (4,5,7,7,9,7,9,6) at level 29, ZERO of 8 sub-attributes reach the 95% ceiling on normal work, and rank 20 lands at -2 against the old formula. The stated failure mode — +10 pushing mid-game characters into the ceiling — does not occur. ⚠️ TESTED AT n=1 because only one deep save exists; the blast radius is small for the same reason (the column is +0 at rank 4, and 6 of 11 real characters never leave early game). ⛔ IT RETIRES attributeSoftCap: the resolver must read rollCumulative here INSTEAD of the min/max formula at resolve.js:73, not in addition to it. Doing both would double-count every roll in the game.

phases._note: Measured from 14 real saves at 25.2 actions/level (SNG-354). Erik corrected 2026-08-07: Silas at lvl 29 is MID tier, not the ceiling.

early.need: base health and energy — the survival floor. 6 of 11 real characters never leave this phase.

mid.need: power, reach, effectiveness. Silas Weir (lvl 29, subs 4-9) lives here.

late.need: world arcs, holdings, company, businesses. PARTIALLY BLOCKED — see _blocked.

deep.need: the cap; reached only in a very long campaign.

_blocked: ⚠️ `rapport` ranks 14–20 remain AUTHORED AS PLACEHOLDERS. ✅ `presence` 14/18/20 were unblocked and authored 2026-09-02 against the shipped holdings model. ⛔ `rapport` still waits on Erik: its late-tier grant is 'household capacity', and household is deliberately not modelled as a holding — so there is nothing to raise until he rules whether the milestone is a cap or a household that endures unattended. `wits` 4/10 also remain blocked pending R7's novel-use build.
_spreadNote: ⚠️ MEASURED: nobody single-stats. Silas spread 29 points across all 8 subs, because the roll reads whichever sub the GM NAMES — a specialist is helpless the moment a different one is called. The ladder must therefore stay worth spreading; if a single sub's late ranks ever dominate, that is a defect.

strength.line: What you can take. Strength is the reserve a body carries into a bad day.

milestones.1: The body holds — you can take a hit and keep standing.
milestones.4: Hardened. You stop being the first one down.
milestones.7: Deep reserve — you outlast fights that should have ended you.
milestones.10: You are hard to finish, and people who have seen you fight say so.
milestones.14: A body that arguments and weather both fail against.
milestones.18: The kind of durability that becomes a reason others follow you into things.
milestones.20: You do not go down. Not from this.

agility.line: What does not land. Agility is the harm that never arrives.

milestones.1: You can get out of the way.
milestones.4: Hard to corner — retreats work, and pursuit costs them.
milestones.7: ⚑ HARM RUNG: a blow that would incapacitate lands one rung lighter.
milestones.10: You are not where the blow went.
milestones.14: ⚑ HARM RUNG: a second rung. What kills others wounds you.
milestones.18: Trouble arrives and finds the space you were in.
milestones.20: You are only hit by things that chose you and were right.

reason.line: What you can spend. Reason is how much craft you have in you before the day is done.

milestones.1: You can work a craft and still walk home.
milestones.4: A full day's work is in reach.
milestones.7: You stop rationing. The craft comes when it is needed.
milestones.10: Depth — you can carry a long working and have something left.
milestones.14: You outlast the problem rather than the other way round.
milestones.18: Sustained work at a scale that changes places.
milestones.20: The reserve is no longer the limit. You are.

insight.line: What you can see coming. Insight is the read on the odds before you commit.

milestones.1: Risky or safe — you can tell that much.
milestones.4: ⚑ SENSE TIER: the five bands. You know roughly how bad this is.
milestones.7: You read WHY, not only how much.
milestones.10: ⚑ SENSE TIER: close numeric read plus reasons. Very little surprises you.
milestones.14: You see the shape of a thing before it has finished becoming it.
milestones.18: The odds are legible even when the situation is not.
milestones.20: You are rarely wrong about what is about to happen.

presence.line: How far your name travels. Presence is what happens in rooms you have not entered yet.

milestones.4: Locally known — your name arrives before you in your own valley.
milestones.10: Renowned — doors open on the name alone.
milestones.14: Your name keeps a place you are not standing in. What you hold does not slip while people remember who holds it.
milestones.18: Standing that governs, not merely opens. People act in your name without being asked, and a place you hold can prosper with nobody assigned to it.
milestones.20: Legendary — the name is a power in the world. A post granted to you owes nothing back; whoever granted it now draws standing from YOUR holding of it, not the reverse.

10.why: ⛔ R25a (ERIK 2026-09-02) — THE FIFTH PLACE AT YOUR SIDE, and the ladder changes hands here. ⚠️ Rapport is who will follow YOU; presence is who will follow a NAME. Rapport carries the first four places (1·4·7·10) and stops; renown carries the fifth and sixth. ✅ Validated against Silas: L30, rapport 7, presence 9 — four in company, exactly at the rapport ceiling with the fifth one rank out of reach. ⛔ The model was not fitted to him; he fell on it.
10.needsWiring: ✅ NONE — `companyPlaces` already reads `companyCapacity` across every sub and takes the highest reached.

14.reads: engine/holdings.js — advanceHolding(): `unstewarded` currently allows Math.min(step,0), so an unkept holding slips on `problem`.
14.effect: An UNSTEWARDED holding of yours cannot fall below `holding`. It still cannot thrive — nobody is there — but it stops decaying.
14.why: ⚠️ This is the milestone text made exact. `presence` governs how far your name travels; at 14 the name reaches a place you are not standing in. ⛔ It does NOT give you a steward — SNG-355's company work stays load-bearing. It only stops the slide.
14.needsWiring: ⬜ CCode: `advanceHolding` clamps the unstewarded floor at CONDITIONS.indexOf('holding') when the character's presence rank ≥ 14.

14.why: ⛔ R25a — THE SIXTH AND LAST PLACE. Cap is 6. ⚠️ THIS RANK IS NOW COMPOUND and the ruling records that as deliberate: presence 14 already carried `unstewardedFloor`, and it keeps it. A name that holds a place you are not standing in is the same name that gathers a sixth person to your side.
14.needsWiring: ✅ NONE — but the ARRAY form is new here (R25a). A rank carrying two effects was unrepresentable before it.

18.effect: The unstewarded ceiling lifts. A holding with no keeper can climb the full ladder to `thriving` on your standing alone.
18.why: ⚠️ The escalation of 14, on the same mechanic: at 14 the name holds a place, at 18 it IMPROVES one. ✅ That is precisely *governs, not merely opens* — renown at 10 opens a door; this does a steward's work at a distance.
18.needsWiring: ⬜ CCode: the `Math.min(next, holding)` clamp is skipped at presence ≥ 18. ⚠️ The `unkept` news string should stop firing too — it reads wrong for a place prospering in your name.

20.reads: engine/holdings.js — the `obligation` field, surfaced by holdingsForGM as `— owes: …`.
20.effect: Obligation on your holdings is discharged by the name alone. `holdingsForGM` stops reporting what you owe and reports what is owed TO the holding for being yours.
20.why: ⛔ THE INVERSION IS THE POINT. A post is granted, and the grant carries a debt to whoever granted it. At 20 that relationship turns over: the granting authority draws standing from your holding of the place. ⚠️ This is a GM-facing and narrative change, not a numeric one — nothing gets +X.
20.needsWiring: ⬜ CCode: `holdingsForGM` inverts the obligation clause at presence ≥ 20. ⚠️ Smallest of the three and mostly a string change.

presence._authored_20260902: ✅ Ranks 14/18/20 authored against the SHIPPED holdings model (`engine/holdings.js`, SNG-358) — the dependency the `_blocked` note was waiting on. ⚠️ All three express against mechanics that already exist: the unstewarded floor, the unstewarded ceiling, and the `obligation` field. ⛔ NONE invents a new engine concept, and none grants a numeric bonus. ⛔ `rapport` 14/18/20 REMAIN BLOCKED — Erik owes a ruling on whether the milestone is a CAP or a household that endures unattended, and CCode notes `rapport`'s 'household capacity' has nothing to raise: household is deliberately NOT a holding kind (`HOLDING_KINDS = ['post','enterprise']`), because 'the moment a pregnant wife grants a combat bonus the game has said something false.'

milestones.7: ⚑ COMPANY: a third. People stay through hard stretches.
milestones.10: ⚑ COMPANY: a fourth. You keep a company rather than collecting one.
milestones.14: ⚑ BLOCKED PENDING HOLDINGS (SNG-358): people in your service you do not travel with.
milestones.18: ⚑ BLOCKED PENDING HOLDINGS: a household, and it holds without you.

The authored line is "people in your service you do not travel with", and that is the DELEGATION scale, not the company one. ✅ It raises delegation capacity by one, on R25b's formula `floor(level/10) + bonus`. ⚠️ It was authored BLOCKED PENDING HOLDINGS; holdings shipped, and R25 supplied the missing half — what standing governs.

Building the penalty so the milestone can remove it would make the game worse to satisfy a line of prose; whether experimentation should cost anything is Erik's design call, not a wiring gap.

_baselineNote: ⛔ SNG-356 CORRECTION 2026-08-07 (found by the SNG-357 harness: Brynjar's maxHealth went 30 -> 62, more than doubling). RANKS 1-2 GRANT NOTHING. Every character begins with sub-attributes at 2 — that is the free starting value, not investment — so granting on ranks 1-2 raised EVERY character's baseline rather than rewarding anyone. The ladder now pays from rank 3, where a point was actually spent. This is why the retroactive preview existed: the harness caught a systematic inflation that looked correct in the table.
_milestoneEffectsNote: ⛔ SNG-390 — THE ⚑ MARKER WAS A HUMAN CONVENTION WITH NO READER. Sixteen milestones across the ladder carry ⚑ to mean 'this one is mechanical, not flavour', and nothing in the engine could tell the difference — so a milestone could promise a mechanic that did not exist and read exactly like one that did. `milestoneEffects` TRANSCRIBES what each ⚑ line already says into a structured form; it invents nothing and adds no new promise. ⚠️ WHERE A MILESTONE NAMES SOMETHING THE ENGINE DOES NOT HAVE, it carries `blocked` with the reason rather than being quietly dropped — an unbuilt promise that is WRITTEN DOWN is a decision waiting to be made; one that is deleted is a lie the player already read.
